content.overview: Article 312 provides that if the Council of States has declared by resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest to do so, Parliament may by law provide for the creation of one or more all-India services common to the Union and the States, and regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to any such service. The IAS and IPS (and existing all-India services) are continued.
content.glance: All-India services: Rajya Sabha resolution (≥2/3 present and voting) → Parliament may by law create AIS common to Union and States and regulate recruitment/conditions. IAS/IPS continued.
content.study:
Article 312 all-India services:
1. Prerequisite: Council of States resolution that creation is necessary or expedient in the national interest, supported by ≥2/3 of members present and voting.
2. Parliament may by law create one or more all-India services common to the Union and the States.
3. Parliament may regulate recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to such services.
4. Continuance of existing IAS and IPS (and other pre-existing all-India services as provided).

Examination: Rajya Sabha special resolution; national interest; common to Union and States; IAS/IPS continuance; link Art 310 (pleasure of President).

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Rajya Sabha resolution (≥2/3 present and voting) that AIS is necessary/expedient in national interest.
2. Parliament may by law create AIS common to Union and States.
3. Regulate recruitment and conditions of service.
4. IAS and IPS continued.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How can an all-India service be created under Article 312?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 312, if the Council of States has declared by resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest to do so, Parliament may by law provide for the creation of one or more all-India services common to the Union and the States and regulate the recruitment and the conditions of service of persons appointed to any such service. The Indian Administrative Service and the Indian Police Service continue as all-India services.

keyTakeaways: Art 312: creation of all-India services via Rajya Sabha resolution + parliamentary law.
